pending_commit.commit_message: UPSTREAM: r8152: disable RX aggregation on Dell TB16 dock r8153 on Dell TB15/16 dock corrupts rx packets. This change is suggested by Realtek. They guess that the XHCI controller doesn't have enough buffer, and their guesswork is correct, once the RX aggregation gets disabled, the issue is gone. ASMedia is currently working on a real sulotion for this issue. Dell and ODM confirm the bcdDevice and iSerialNumber is unique for TB16. Note that TB15 has different bcdDevice and iSerialNumber, which are not unique values. If you still have TB15, please contact Dell to replace it with TB16. BugLink: https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1729674 Cc: Mario Limonciello <mario.limonciello@dell.com> Signed-off-by: Kai-Heng Feng <kai.heng.feng@canonical.com> Signed-off-by: David S. UPSTREAM: r8152: fix wrong checksum status for received IPv4 packets The device could only check the checksum of TCP and UDP packets. Therefore, for the IPv4 packets excluding TCP and UDP, the check of checksum is necessary, even though the IP checksum is correct. Take ICMP for example, The IP checksum may be correct, but the ICMP checksum may be wrong. Signed-off-by: Hayes Wang <hayeswang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit ea6499e160a74ea813e53e7bef2ccb22df1e4929) Signed-off-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:897895 TEST=test_that $IP BootPerf TEST=test_that $IP network_EthernetStressPlug --args num_iterations=1000,interface=eth0 Change-Id: I52df297598d51da59d7641db05401a648c72a7b6 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1330672 Tested-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hayes Wang <hayeswang@realtek.com>

UPSTREAM: r8152: set rx mode early when linking on Set rx mode before calling netif_wake_queue() when linking on to avoid the device missing the receiving packets. The transmission may start after calling netif_wake_queue(), and the packets of resopnse may reach before calling rtl8152_set_rx_mode() which let the device could receive packets. Then, the packets of response would be missed. Signed-off-by: Hayes Wang <hayeswang@realtek.com> Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net> (cherry picked from commit aece4770fba62102951891c2f349a255c83eacb9) Signed-off-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> BUG=chromium:897895 TEST=test_that $IP BootPerf TEST=test_that $IP network_EthernetStressPlug --args num_iterations=1000,interface=eth0 Change-Id: I7547e0f3743159fa73ca45207811513e73fed3ec Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1330673 Tested-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Grant Grundler <grundler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hayes Wang <hayeswang@realtek.com>

UPSTREAM: net: usb: r8152: use irqsave() in USB's complete callback The USB completion callback does not disable interrupts while acquiring the lock. We want to remove the local_irq_disable() invocation from __usb_hcd_giveback_urb() and therefore it is required for the callback handler to disable the interrupts while acquiring the lock. The callback may be invoked either in IRQ or BH context depending on the USB host controller. Use the _irqsave() variant of the locking primitives. Cc: "David S. CHROMIUM: bluetooth: determine wide band speech by controller id This patch creates a blacklist for controllers that do not support the wide band speech capability. For Intel controllers, the Stone Peak 2 or older ones do not support the capability. Any newer ones should support it by default. Note that only Intel newer controllers support the capability for now. We will add other vendors to support it later. BUG=chromium:970946 TEST=None. Add kerberosd to password-viewers Allows the Kerberos daemon to access the Chrome OS login password stored in the kernel keyring. The login password will be used when admins specify the placeholder '${PASSWORD}' in the KerberosAccounts policy. kerberos: Add modes to ClearAccounts call Adds 2 more modes to ClearAccounts(). Besides clearing everything, one can now clear unmanaged accounts only as well as stored passwords for unmanaged accounts. Clearing unmanaged accounts is needed when the KerberosAddAccountsAllowed policy is turned off. In that case, Chrome removes all previously added unmanaged accounts. Managed accounts are kept. Similarly, clearing passwords for unmanaged accounts is needed when the KerberosRememberPasswordEnabled policy is set to false. In that case, Chrome removes all previously stored passwords for unmanaged accounts. Managed passwords are kept. tast.video.*Perf: Improve CPU measurement logic for performance tests. This CL improves the CPU measurement logic used in Tast performance tests: - MeasureProcessCPU will no longer write the measured CPU usage to disk. This is error prone and makes it very difficult to reuse this function. - A duration parameter is added to MeasureProcessCPU so each tests can specify a different measurement duration. - The logic to cleanup a process after measurement has been improved, reducing the change of a process not properly being killed. - Extract SetUpBenchmark from MeasureProcessCPU, to avoid being called multiple times when doing multiple measurements. The testcase is now responsible for properly setting up benchmark mode. - SetUpBenchmark no longer returns a context. It is sometimes necessary to have a shorter context even before calling SetUpBenchmark, so this is the reponsibility of the test case. - DisableCPUFrequencyScaling and DisableThermalThrottling are made private.
